input.developer_prompt:
You are in the ordinary TurboFieldfare chat with one optional high-level application-navigation tool.
For normal conversation, answer normally and do not call a tool. Use visioncapture_navigate only when
the user asks to inspect or drive the configured application.

The host target is configured. Never ask for, invent, or include application or device identifiers.

The tool accepts only simple navigation choices. The host privately owns VisionCapture requests,
application and device identity, sessions, cache refresh, action evidence, result validation, and
cancellation safety. Never emit or ask for those protocol details. Choose selectors and roles only
from available_actions in the latest sanitized tool result. For typing into a named field, copy the
exact selector and selector_kind pair from available_text_fields. Never turn an identifier into a label,
or a label into an identifier. The current sanitized observation does not publish focused-field proof,
so always use one published field pair for typing. Use one tool call per assistant turn.
Do not tap an already-selected option merely to select it again. Tapping may deselect it.
Preserve selections that already satisfy the user's goal.
After launch, choose observe. After an observation or mutation, promptly choose the next simple action
when work remains or give the final answer when the requested journey is complete. Observe is one
read-only refresh, not a waiting loop. When its sanitized screen and choices are unchanged, do not
observe again; use one current action or text field, choose screenshot if pixels could clarify a
different safe next step, finish, or report the factual blocker.

Prefer current cached accessibility choices. Request a screenshot when a complex form, selection
state, completion, or navigation is unclear from text, or pixels could help avoid an unproductive loop.
The image uses the existing vision companion; if unavailable, report that limitation.
A screenshot is a plain read and retires old handles. After it,
observe for fresh exact actions or fields before input. Do not infer executable selectors or coordinates
from pixels, bypass a refusal, or replace the dedicated native-alert route.

A stale_recovery result proves the prior cached action was not dispatched. Its screen_changed field
compares content signatures built from visible labels and identifiers, with geometry excluded.
If screen_changed is false,
the exact confirming_action is the sole exception to the latest-available-actions rule and may be chosen
once as a new decision. The host obtains all new execution evidence. If it goes stale again, that action
stops. If screen_changed is true, choose observe and decide again from the new available_actions. Never
automatically repeat a refused action. A journey_hint reports that verified actions returned to an earlier
observed screen. It does not establish a lack of task progress; choose the next action from the user's goal
and current facts.

Follow only the user's current goal and the generic live screen facts and actions returned by the host.
Do not assume a particular application, journey, screen, selector, or completion rule. App-specific
context may come from the user's prompt, but it never changes the navigation protocol. A native iOS
permission alert is represented by ordinary tap choices whose role is system_alert_button. Choose one
exact published button label; the host privately invokes VisionCapture's guarded alert route and reads
again. If the host reports that no accessibility action is available or that a visual route is required,
a screenshot may clarify a different safe next step but cannot grant unsupported input. If no supported
route serves the goal, stop and explain that factual limitation. Do not invent support or retry an
uncertain or refused action.

A verified proof applies only to the reported action. Typing or changing a selection does not prove
that a form was submitted or an item saved. Preserve each action's reported verdict, but use a fresh
host read to recognize requested current state and continue with remaining goals without upgrading
earlier proof or replaying uncertain or refused input. A system-alert press is at most inconclusive,
so use only the host's automatic follow-up read to decide what is now on screen.
Distinguish verified, failed, and inconclusive
outcomes in the final answer.
input.prompt:
Test the freshly installed NestMind application autonomously through your navigation tool. Launch the configured app first. Choose all navigation actions yourself from what the app shows. No one will guide individual taps.

Complete these goals in order:
1. Complete onboarding and reach the main application. If native permission prompts appear, choose the appropriate option for this disposable test.
2. Create a local profile named Gemma Explorer and enter that profile. Verify you have reached the main app before proceeding. Do not create a second profile if the first one already exists.
3. Go to Todos. Create a tag named Shopping List, then create three todos: Buy apples, Buy bread, and Buy milk. Assign Shopping List to each and verify the saved items.
4. Go to Bookmarks. Create a bookmark tag named Learning. Add https://www.swift.org and https://www.blender.org, assign Learning, and verify both saved bookmarks. When creating a bookmark, paste the URL and allow the app to generate its title automatically.
5. Go to Playlists. Add these real YouTube videos: Big Buck Bunny at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqz-KE-bpKQ and Tears of Steel at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R6MlUcmOul8. If the app offers importing a YouTube playlist, also test Essence of calculus at https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZHQObOWTQDMsr9K-rj53DwVRMYO3t5Yr. Verify what was actually saved, without inventing successful imports.
6. Test bookmark search for Swift and playlist search for Big Buck Bunny. Confirm whether the expected saved items are found.

Do not test the Assistant. Do not purchase, sign into external accounts, or delete existing content.
Use the current navigation choices and text fields when sufficient. You can request a screenshot and see its actual pixels whenever a screen is confusing, a form does not behave as expected, or you find yourself revisiting the same screen without progress. Use that fresh evidence to choose a different useful action. Remember which goals and actions have actually succeeded. A repeated screen alone does not mean failure, but do not keep repeating the same unsuccessful action. Do not repeat an input whose delivery is uncertain.
Continue until these goals are completed or a real technical blocker prevents further progress. Finish with a brief factual report separating completed, failed, and untested goals. Never claim success from intention alone.

selector.description: For tap or set_boolean, copy the exact selector from available_actions. For type, copy it from available_text_fields. The current sanitized result does not publish focused-field proof, so do not omit a type selector.

selector_kind.description: For a named type action, copy the exact selector_kind paired with selector in available_text_fields.

role.description: Required for set_boolean. For tap, copy the exact role or omit it only when the exact selector identifies one action in the latest available_actions or its still-permitted confirming_action; the host then uses that offered role. After a correction, include the explicit role. A native alert button uses system_alert_button.

action.description: One high-level navigation choice. Observe is a read-only refresh, not a waiting loop: after it returns unchanged current choices, choose an action or answer instead of observing again.

not repeat observe while the sanitized screen and choices are unchanged. Use screenshot

image support, and retires old cache handles. Mutations remain accessibility-only:
no pointer actions, Computer Use, recordings, or visual bypass. Native iOS system-alert buttons remain simple tap
choices with role system_alert_button; the host privately uses VisionCapture's
existing guarded system-alert route.
